conviction_note: Peers that reported after Frontline last spoke (DHT, Okeanis, INSW) all beat their own Q2-call Q3 bookings and consensus and were bought +3.6 to +4.9%, and Frontline's Q2 consensus beat was bought only +1.0%; against that, VLCC spot has fallen ~64% from the 8 Oct peak, the stock is -13% over 20 days with 23 vol points of put skew, and the Q3 consensus is disputed ($2.29 vs $1.98). The findings sum to +1.1. The scaled number is +0.44 (p_up 54 x abs 5.5) because the bar is disputed and the sign runs against the skew, so p_up stays close to 50.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS consensus $2.29 / revenue $723.2m (Chartmill, via search snippet; https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/FRO/estimates; FY2026 consensus $9.02, 11 analysts, as of 2026-10-31), against $1.98 at Bullstory (https://bullstory.io/en/stocks/fro/earnings/2026-q3). The two sources disagree, so the bar is treated as disputed and the reported-quarter finding is capped small. Company guide: Q3 spot TCE booked VLCC $156,900 (86%), Suezmax $117,400 (79%), LR2 $81,000 (70%), with full-quarter TCEs expected below these because of ballast days (https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/fro-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-results, 2026-08-28). Q2 adj EPS was $2.61.
positioning_check: Short interest 10,303,024 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, up 1.21m, 2.20 days to cover per FINRA via Equibles (https://equibles.com/stocks/fro/short-interest); its summary page shows about 4.9% of float and 3.5 days. Not a crowded short. Baseline: 25d skew +22.98 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.48, ATM IV 70.9%, but the ATM spread is 82% of mid, so there is no usable implied move. Run-up -5.1% over 5 days and -13.3% over 20; -25% from the 52-week high; roughly -20% month to date in November (high $55.62, low $42.19).

findings.finding: Tanker peers that reported Q3 2026 after Frontline's 28 Aug call beat both their own Q2-call Q3 bookings and consensus by wide margins: Okeanis (ECO) adj EPS $7.67 vs $4.84 consensus, VLCC Q3 spot $269,300 vs about $207,000 booked at the Q2 call; DHT EPS $1.68 vs $1.30 (+29%), Q3 VLCC spot $167,100/day; INSW revenue 22% above expectations on VLCC spot $154,600. Frontline guided Q3 VLCC at $156,900 on 86% of days and warned the full quarter would come in lower, and Q3 consensus ($1.98-2.29) sits below Q2's $2.61 adj EPS. That points to a Q3 beat of the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: EPS $2.96 vs $2.74 consensus (+8%), stock +1.01% post-earnings (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/FRO/q2-2026/). Q3 2025: adj EPS $0.19 vs about $0.24 estimate, stock fell 6.7% over the following week (https://finviz.com/news/240535/frontline-plc-fro-falls-after-missing-profit-estimates-in-q3). Peer reactions to Q3 2026 beats: DHT +4.91%, ECO +3.58%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus aggregators still show a Q3 bar below Q2's $2.61 adj EPS, which suggests estimates were anchored on Frontline's own ballast-day warning rather than on peers' Q3 outturns. Had the beat been priced, the stock would have tracked the peers' post-print gains instead of falling about 20% in November. The weight is low because the bar is disputed and Frontline's Q3 VLCC guide already trailed ECO's.
findings.independence: DHT beat consensus: https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/DHT/q3-2026/ (2026-11-14). INSW revenue beat: https://247wallst.com/cards/international-seaways-q3-2026-earnings-insw-01m6nve1df8akxbqz9dh9pn5eg. These are peer proxies, not Frontline's own number.

findings.finding: Peers' Q4-to-date bookings are multiples of Q3: ECO has 48% of VLCC spot days at $688,800 and 60% of Suezmax days at $410,900, about $480m of revenue secured against Q3's $338m; DHT has 68% of VLCC spot days at about $579,900. Frontline's Q4-to-date bookings, which it publishes in the release, should likewise point to a record Q4 and a Q4 dividend well above Q3, while FY2026 consensus of $9.02 (as of 31 Oct) implies a modest H2. Frontline also has a larger fleet, with newbuild VLCCs delivering from Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: DHT, guiding Q4 above Q3 on $579,900 VLCC bookings, closed +4.9%. ECO, with huge Q4 bookings, +3.6%, with the CEO warning against extrapolating to open days. Frontline's Q2 call (Q3 bookings above Q2 levels) bought +1.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector Q4 numbers are public, so most of this is priced. What may not be is the size of Frontline's own Q4 implied EPS and dividend against a $44 stock that fell 20% this month. One source says owner share prices imply about $55,000/day VLCC averages in 2027, so the market is pricing the forward curve, not the quarter. If it were priced, consensus Q4 and FY numbers would already have stepped up to peer-implied levels, and FY $9.02 suggests they have not.
findings.independence: ECO Q4 bookings: https://finviz.com/news/421910/okeanis-eco-tankers-doubles-consensus-and-locks-in-a-huge-q4-but-the-rate-peak-may-already-be-behind-it (2026-11-12). FY consensus via the Chartmill snippet. Shares the peer-print documents with the Q3 finding, but lands on a different line (Q4 bookings vs reported Q3).

findings.finding: A meaningful part of Frontline's VLCC fleet is on fixed time charters far below Q4 spot: seven VLCCs on one-year charters at $76,900/day (from Jan-Apr 2026), two newbuilds at $120,000 for one year, and two 2016-built VLCCs at $90,000 (two years) and $75,000 (three years). That dilutes Frontline's Q4 relative to spot-heavy peers like ECO.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Frontline's Q3 VLCC guide ($156,900) already trailed ECO's Q2-call Q3 booking (about $207,000).
findings.why_not_priced: These charters are public, so they are largely priced. The residual is that a reader mapping ECO/DHT Q4 bookings onto Frontline will overstate its Q4 fleetwide TCE, and the release will show the blended number.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 release lists the newbuild and 2016-built VLCC charters: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/fro-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-results

findings.finding: VLCC spot rates have collapsed since the 8 Oct record: Gulf of Oman-China fell about 64% to 308 Worldscale by 13 Nov (Baltic Exchange), TD3C earnings fell 17.9% week on week to $1.06m/day, Atlantic routes fell harder (TD22 -16.2%, Suezmax TD20 -46.6%, Aframax TD19 -69.8% in the week to 6 Nov), and Kpler/Vortexa expect further drift lower as tonnage frees up. Management's commentary on open Q4 days and Q1 2027 will be struck at these lower levels.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ECO's CEO warned against extrapolating Q4 bookings to open days at about $350,000 (VLCC); the stock still closed +3.6%. Tanker equities have fallen with rates through November.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock is -13% over 20 days and about -20% in November, and the put skew is +23 vol points, which is how it looks when it is priced. The residual is that Frontline's call may quantify a Q1 2027 exit rate below what the tape implies, given its Atlantic-heavy trading and its CEO's stated choice not to position for a Gulf reopening.

findings.finding: Capital return: Frontline pays out roughly its adjusted EPS each quarter (Q2 dividend $2.61 = adj EPS) and announced a $0.80 special dividend from the $270m sale of two 2017-built VLCCs, delivery expected in Q3. The Q3 declaration (about $2.0-2.7 ordinary plus $0.80 special if the sale closed) is about a 6-8% quarterly yield on $44.39.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's $2.61 plus $0.80 special announcement: +1.0% on the day, then +4.4% over the following week (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/FRO/q2-2026/).
findings.why_not_priced: The policy and the special are public. The only unpriced part is the exact ordinary dividend, which follows the Q3 beat or miss, so most of this rides on the Q3 finding.
findings.independence: The Q2 release confirms the special is subject to closing: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/fro-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-results. Partly overlaps the Q3 finding through the payout.

findings.finding: The two 2017-built VLCCs sold for $270m in total (about $179m net cash) were due to deliver in Q3. The sale gain will lift reported (GAAP) EPS above adjusted EPS (Q2 carried a $54.7m Suezmax sale gain), so headline EPS may screen as a larger beat against aggregator consensus than the adjusted figure supports.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GAAP $2.96 vs $2.74 consensus was scored as a beat (+1.0%), although adj EPS was $2.61. DHT's $34.2m sale gain likewise inflated its headline beat.
findings.why_not_priced: It is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction of the same dollars. The effect is headline mechanics only: wire screens comparing GAAP EPS with consensus.
findings.independence: Q2 release on the gain precedent: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/fro-second-quarter-and-six-months-2026-results

findings.finding: Positioning into the print: FRO is down about 20% month to date and 13.3% over 20 days, with short interest rising 1.2m shares to 10.3m (about 4.9% of float, 2.2 days to cover, 15 Oct settlement), while peers DHT and ECO were bought on their Q3 prints in the same rate tape.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peers' Q3 2026 prints during the November rate decline: DHT +4.9%, ECO +3.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference. The de-rating and the bid for puts mean expectations are low going in, so a print in line with peers has room to be bought. It is a modest short, not crowded, so this is not a squeeze mechanism.
findings.independence: Month-to-date price range via search snippet: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/FRO. Peer reactions: https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/DHT/q3-2026/

findings.finding: Danske Bank and DZ Bank cut Frontline to Sell in August 2026 (Danske target $39.15), while BTIG raised its target to $70. The street is split, with an average target around $54.
findings.why_not_priced: Three months old, so priced. It is filed only because it bears on how a Q4 guide is received by the bears.

baseline_tension: The positive lean (peer beats bought, a Q3 beat likely, record Q4 bookings) cuts against the +23-vol-point put skew and the -13% 20-day run-up. The reason given for overriding the skew is that peers printing into the same rate collapse were bought +3.6 to +4.9%; the skew number is also suspect because the chain is wide (82% ATM spread). The tension keeps p_up at 54.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar disputed, $2.29 vs $1.98): Q3 beat finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6
Lesson 5 (peer proxy, not company number) plus lesson 1 (FRO's own Q2 beat bought only +1.0%): Q4 bookings finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong put skew): p_up moved from 55 to 54, with an explicit reason in baseline_tension; abs_move left at 5.5
